title: Office Cleaning Frequency Newcastle: Build a Schedule Around Your Working Week

excerpt: Plan office cleaning around actual attendance, amenities, visitors and access. Use a practical task matrix and a four-week review instead of guessing from desk numbers.
body:
## How often should an office be cleaned?

There is no single visit frequency that suits every office. Start with the areas used, the tasks required and when a problem needs attention. A busy shared kitchen may need staff attention during the day as well as an agreed cleaning visit. A lightly used meeting room may need a different pattern. One frequency for the entire building can hide both gaps and unnecessary work.

For workplaces in Newcastle CBD and Lake Macquarie, a useful brief records a representative working week before asking for a price. It is a planning exercise, not a hygiene assessment or a prescribed minimum standard.

[Discuss your workplace cleaning schedule](/cleaning#cleaning-quote-form)

## Step 1: record use, not just headcount

Count who actually attends on each day, including visitors, training groups and contractors. Note lunch periods, meeting-room bookings and closing times. A hybrid office can be quiet on Friday and full on Tuesday; an average headcount does not describe either day particularly well.

Record recurring issues and when they appear. An overflowing bin at 2 pm needs a different response from a scheduled task missed overnight. Do not record staff health information or personal movements to prepare this brief. Approximate occupancy and shared-area use are enough.

## Step 2: separate three types of responsibility

- **Between visits:** staff or another nominated person manage spills, food waste and agreed resets as they occur. Confirm how urgent hazards are reported.
- **Routine service:** the provider completes the tasks and visit pattern set out in the written scope.
- **Periodic or specialist work:** carpet extraction, high-level access or other detail work needs its own frequency, safe method, responsibility and price where applicable.

A scheduled cleaner is not automatically responsible for every incident between visits. Equally, staff tidying does not replace a task included in the cleaning contract. Write the boundary down.

## Step 3: use this office cleaning frequency matrix

The examples below are discussion prompts, not a recommended schedule for every workplace. Complete the actual frequency after a site inspection and consultation with the people responsible for the workplace.

On smaller screens, scroll the table sideways to read every column.

| Area | What to observe | Routine task to agree | Between-visit responsibility | Review trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Entry and reception | Visitor peaks, tracked-in material, presentation | Accessible surfaces, bins and floor care | Spills and unexpected hazards | More visitors or recurring floor issues |
| Kitchens and break rooms | Meal use, food waste, shared appliances | Agreed surfaces, sinks, bins and floors | Personal dishes and immediate spill response | Events, odours or overflowing waste |
| Toilets and amenities | Use across the working day | Agreed fixtures, surfaces and floors | Report problems and agreed replenishment | Supplies running out or unmet standards |
| Workstations | Attendance and accessible desk space | Agreed accessible surfaces and floors | Clear desks; protect confidential material | Layout or attendance changes |
| Meeting and training rooms | Booking intensity and catering | Tables, bins and floors as scoped | Between-session resets | Back-to-back bookings or larger groups |
| Glass and floor detail work | Finish instructions and condition | Separately defined periodic tasks | Report damage and maintenance needs | Wear, changed surfaces or access restrictions |

For each row add the scheduled days, time window, acceptance standard and task owner. Avoid vague instructions such as “as needed” without saying who decides, who approves extra work and how it is charged.

## Step 4: test the schedule against your budget

Ask providers to price the same task list. Compare visit frequency, estimated workload, consumables responsibilities, periodic work, access constraints and GST treatment. A lower weekly amount may leave more tasks to your staff or exclude work you assumed was included.

Do not reduce a required task solely to reach a target price. Discuss priorities and feasible alternatives with the provider, and check applicable workplace requirements with the appropriate adviser. Our [cleaning cost comparison guide](/blog/commercial-cleaning-cost-newcastle) includes a worked annual comparison.

## Step 5: review a representative four-week period

Agree a review point rather than assuming the first schedule will stay right forever. Four weeks is an example planning window, not a YOS service guarantee. Record whether tasks were completed, whether access was available and whether the result met the agreed standard.

Separate missed work from changed requirements. If a scheduled kitchen task was missed, resolve delivery. If the kitchen meets the overnight standard but becomes overloaded by midday, review use and daytime responsibilities. The remedy is different.

Our [quality review guide](/blog/what-good-commercial-cleaning-looks-like) explains how to record an issue clearly. The [busier office scope guide](/blog/commercial-cleaning-scope-busier-office) helps when attendance or activities have changed.

## Cleaning schedule checklist for your next quote

1. Record attendance and visitor patterns across the week.
2. List each area and the tasks required there.
3. Nominate between-visit responsibilities.
4. Agree days, timing, access and the standard for each scheduled task.
5. Identify consumables, periodic work and exclusions.
6. Compare equivalent scopes and total costs.
7. Agree how issues and extra work are approved.
8. Set a review date and record any agreed changes in writing.

[Download the editable planning template](/guides/office-cleaning-planning-template.txt)

The template contains no client examples or preset price promises. You can also use our existing [cleaning scope pack (PDF)](/guides/workplace-cleaning-scope-checklist.pdf).
